heroHeadline: Trump Administration Dismantles Ocean Observatories Initiative; Oceana Sues Over Gulf ESA Rollback Including Rice's Whale as Mombasa Ocean Summit Approaches
heroSubtitle: The Trump administration announced plans to shut down the $368 million Ocean Observatories Initiative (OOI) — a 900-sensor network monitoring the AMOC, deep-sea temperatures, and Cascadia seismics — with the first physical buoy removal confirmed off Oregon on June 4, 2026. Simultaneously, Oceana and Earthjustice filed suit on June 3 over an ESA 'God Squad' exemption stripping protections from 20 Gulf of Mexico species including the critically endangered Rice's whale (fewer than 100 individuals), to facilitate offshore drilling expansion. With the 11th Our Ocean Conference (OOC11) opening in Mombasa, Kenya on June 16 — the first ever held in Africa — NOAA warned of elevated bleaching risk for Hawaii, Florida, and the Caribbean this summer as El Niño rapidly develops; gray whale deaths along Washington's coast extended into June as the eastern Pacific population holds at roughly half its 2016 levels; and Woods Hole researchers unveiled a new coral bleaching prediction method providing five to six months of advance warning to reef managers.
